utterances.text: In January/February this year, you were in contact with the Prosecution with a view to make arrangements for your testimony at the beginning of this case; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you took various steps in order to be able to travel; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you clarify that question? I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you take steps so that you would be able to travel?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But then -- but then on the 21st of February, you sent a letter to the Prosecution, informing the Prosecution that you wanted to be a Defence witness?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So you had changed your mind at this point in time, had you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for the witness. I would at this point respectfully request the admission of the witness's -- the witness's three statements that we have been going through today. It is, as I indicated yesterday, our submission that the witness has been adverse to telling the truth, as he has set it out correctly earlier on in his three consecutive statements to the OTP. The witness has cooperated with the Prosecution, given three statements which he signed, which were read back to him or even read by himself, to which he had the possibility to make corrections, as Your Honours have heard about. Your Honours have heard about the procedure that brought about these statements in a safe manner. The witness provided various documents voluntarily to the Prosecution. The witness was on the Prosecution's witness list to testify at the beginning of the year as of first -- the early batch of witnesses in this case, and spoke to the Prosecution about travel arrangements to come and travel here. And then in February -- in the end of February, the witness stopped communicating with OTP and stated that he was a Defence witness. And as Your Honours know, various other procedural steps had to be taken in order to secure the witness's presence today. But it is our submission that it has become clear during the testimony of the witness that the witness's earlier statements are reliable reflections of his evidence, and on this basis we seek the admission of the three statements pursuant to Rule 89(C), so that this material is before Your Honours to assess the credibility of the witness evidence. It's of course to the Judges to give weight to the testimony and the statements at an appropriate time; but we submit that Your Honours should have these statements in evidence and that Your Honours can rely on the substance of these statements when the time comes to deliberate in this case. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Marcussen. The Trial Chamber will listen to the cross-examination, and we will render a decision regarding the admission of these three written statements. Mr. Seselj, you have three [as interpreted] more hours -- or you have three [as interpreted] hours, rather. Let's not waste any time. You have the floor. I'm sorry, you have two hours, not three hours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, can I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. The transcript has to be corrected. I said Mr. Seselj has two hours and not three, as it states here. Very well. This being done, what did you want to say, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying to the Honourable Trial Chamber that the Prosecutor did not state correctly what all the measures were that were taken and what all the pressures exerted were for me to come here to testify. I had 30 to 50 telephone calls per day. Problems were created for me at work in Serbia, in general, and problems with my family, personally. These are enormous pressures. That can be established easily by way of the telephone. Somebody would call and introduce themselves, saying they were from The Hague Tribunal, somebody else from the Registry, somebody else from the OTP. I mean, really. And that hurt my health.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding this pressure, it was before February or after, or after -- or, rather, the Prosecutor told us that after February, you ceased any contact with the OTP. Is that right? Do you confirm that as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I confirm that, because my team of lawyers received the real statement, that is to say, the one that I am denying here and saying that the OTP reprocessed it in order to suit somebody's needs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's very unusual, but we'll look into this. You were a protected witness. Your lawyer, your attorney, should not have received this statement, but I will address this issue later with my colleagues. But that's another matter altogether. I wanted to know something. So these pressures were exerted on you, and this was done before February; is that right? When did they start? You said that you would receive 30 to 50 phone calls a day. When did all that begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madame Judge, it wasn't before February, it was before the new year. That's when it started, December 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, in February, if I understood correctly, and please correct me if I'm wrong, during the first weeks of this year, you had contacts with the OTP in order to take the necessary steps for you to come to The Hague; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And notwithstanding this pressure, these repeated phone calls that exerted so much pressure on you, you nevertheless had contacts with them in order to come to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to state my views regarding the request of the Prosecution to have this admitted into evidence. Should I do that straight away or after the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can do it -- you have two more hours -- or, rather, you have two hours, so you may use your time as you see fit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I'm not going to use all of two hours. I'm just going to put a few brief questions. But first of all I would like to remind you that it is absolutely inappropriate, from the view of the interests of justice, to have admitted into evidence statements that were prepared by the OTP, itself, and that the witness cannot confirm to be his own in the courtroom. So far, about 35 witnesses were heard here, excluding the experts, and practically in each and every one of these cases, there was a problem; namely, that in the statement that was composed by the OTP, there was something that the witness had not said. I would like to remind you of the case of Goran Stoparic, whose statement contained that when arriving at the rally in Sid, I greeted those present with Hitler's salute, and so on and so forth. There was a big group of witnesses with the same problem. I refer to something in the trial of Slobodan Milosevic. There were 48 witnesses who testified in court quite opposite to what was stated in the statements that were composed for them by the OTP. In every case in every trial, this crops up. Mrs. Lattanzi can confirm that that happened in the Rasim Delic case that she was involved in, too. So this appears everywhere, which shows what the methodology of the OTP's work is. That is why I am absolutely opposed to that. None of the things written by the OTP can be admitted into evidence. As for what's written in the Prosecution statements, I can cross-examine the members of the OTP who wrote up these statements. Now I'm going to move on to the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I'm just going to put a few brief questions to you. Do you remember the meeting with Paolo Pastore-Stocchi and Daniel Saxon on the 21st of June, 2006?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was that in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How long did the meeting last?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Briefly, because Mr. Paolo was in a hurry to catch a plane.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you tell me approximately how long it lasted?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not longer than 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, I would just like to draw your attention to these 20 minutes. Compare it to what was said this morning, that the meeting lasted all day until the evening hours, and then you will see -- well, and I did not have an opportunity to get in touch with this witness since Daniel Saxon testified in court. I did not have an opportunity to speak to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were you given a text in advance that you were supposed to sign?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, it was read out from the laptop. That was very fast. I had to wait for a few minutes for it to be printed out, while I had a cup of coffee, and then I signed -- or, rather, initialled that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was an explanation provided to you then why the OTP, on the basis of your two alleged previous statements, made a single statement and asked you to sign it yet again?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were you told that they would apply Rule 89(F)? That means that your statement would be admitted into evidence without you having to come to The Hague at all.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted). So for the forum, we should also move back into private session. In fact, no, I'm going to ask the Registrar to redact the beginning of the question, of your question, and then we will go then into private session in order for you to be able to put questions regarding this particular line of questioning. So, Mr. Registrar, please, let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, then I'm not going to discuss it any further. I don't want to deal with anything in private session with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, after that, it was 2007. Throughout 2007, did you have any contact with The Hague OTP?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall. I think towards the end of the year, I received these calls to come here for proofing and for preparations for the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The end of 2007?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 2007, that's what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And until then, you had no idea what was contained in your statements?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What was it that influenced you that at one point in time you decided that you didn't want to be a Prosecution witness?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I believe -- well, after all, I'm an intellectual and I understand some things. I understand that something was wrong. Enormous pressure was being exerted for me to come here. And during your trial, nobody told me that I would be a witness against you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you follow my trial during the first days?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few times, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: For example, did you watch the testimony of Goran Stoparic that was in January?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe. Maybe, perhaps 15 or 20 minutes, I'd switch channels.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So following the beginning of my trial did not influence you in terms of giving up on testifying here?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to put this to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And during 2008 --

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: -- did you spend some time in hospital?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My state of health became worse precisely because the threats became more frequent, and also the gentlemen from the OTP were calling me, and you can see that from my medical files.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you say that to the doctors who were treating you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I did not talk about that. I just reported because I said I was sick.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What did the threats consist of?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as for the OTP, it wasn't threats, it was pressure; that I had to come here to testify. Well, once or twice would have been okay, but it happened every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they tell you what would happen if you refused to testify?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That not responding to a court would result in my being sentenced to prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was any pressure ever exerted against you from my side?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: My legal advisers, that is to say, my associates from the Defence team, did they exert any pressure against you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did anybody else during the course of this year exert any kind of pressure against you so that you -- in terms of you not being a Prosecution witness, but rather a Defence witness?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you do that purely through your own free will?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through my own free will, at the moment when I received the entire documentation, that is to say, the entire record that totally astounded me, some of the facts that I referred to, I mean, where I was involved in the war and then it turned out that I wasn't, born in 1966 rather than 1986. I was so astonished by my statement that, I mean, some facts quite simply are not truthful and do not correspond to my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have spoken to us about pressure exerted by the OTP on you. You also mentioned threats which you received. You told us you did not know where these threats came from. I would like to understand more about this, about the threats. The issues about the pressure is sufficiently clear. Now, what were all these threats? Not where they came from because you have already told us that you didn't know where these threats came from. Now, what were all these threats about?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The contents of these threats was that I was a traitor of Serbian people, and a few other threats like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you were told that you were a traitor to the Serb people. Why ?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It upset me so much that it even upset my family. I even had to change my apartment. The address that is stated here is not the address. I live at a completely different address in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you think that people knew that you were in contact with this Tribunal to come and testify on behalf of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor, do you have any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness, on behalf of the Bench, I'd like to thank you for having come to testify during these two days, and I wish you a safe journey home. I shall ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, we shall resume this court case on the 26th of August, if I'm not mistaken. We did not have any list of witnesses. Will we have this list soon?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we will make efforts to provide you with that list as quickly as we can. I believe arrangements are being made with various witnesses to line them up for after the recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, as far as the issue you raised yesterday is concerned, i.e., the search of your cell, prison management has told us, via an e-mail, that an investigation is underway, and we'll be informed about what happened. I cannot, at this stage, answer your question, but we shall be kept abreast of this. A second issue which I would like to deal with quickly. Yesterday, I mentioned an e-mail which Mr. Zoran Krasic sent to the Parliament in Belgrade. (redacted), and in this e-mail, in Cyrillic, there was an insult. This e-mail contained an insult. What happened, exactly? Was it Mr. Krasic who included this in his e-mail or was it someone who added this in when this was transferred electronically? I don't know. Whatever the case may be, the e-mail has been given to you, so perhaps you can ask Mr. Krasic more about this. I have material proof of these insulting words.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already investigated the matter in detail. I tried to tell you about it last night already, and I handed over to the representative of the Registry two photographs that show sent messages and a folder with deleted messages on Zoran Krasic's computer. First of all, Zoran Krasic states categorically that yesterday he had absolutely no contact with The Hague Tribunal, not with the Registry, not with the OTP. Also, that he never had any contact with the representatives of the Registry before that, either. The first photograph that I submitted yesterday, and it can be put on the ELMO because the Registry has it, shows the messages sent from Krasic's computer. In his office, Zoran Krasic, in his office at the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia, he has a computer that he uses, and in that photograph one can see that the last message that was sent by Zoran Krasic is dated the 8th of July, 2008, at 11.38. And the following words can be seen: "From Zoran Krasic," meaning that Zoran Krasic sent the message. In the lower right-hand corner of the first photograph, you can see the date, the 22nd of July, 2008, and the time when it was copied, that is, 1702 hours in the afternoon, after I called Krasic on the phone during the break and asked for detailed information. The second photograph shows deleted messages. That folder is empty. In the lower right-hand corner of the second picture, you can see the date, the 22nd of July, 2008, and the time of copying the picture, 1702 hours. So Zoran Krasic did not send a single e-mail on the 22nd of July, 2008. Zoran Krasic has no idea as to who the official of the Registry is, the one whose name is mentioned here. Is there any reason for her name not to be mentioned? I have no reason to insist on mentioning her name. Should it remain protected? He never heard of a person under that name, never. So this is absolutely impossible. Now, what happened? Was anything sent from the Assembly? Did someone from the Registry try to reach Zoran Krasic in some way? That is something that the Registry should explain to us now. Were they looking for someone via e-mail and was this the answer that they got, or were they totally inactive; did they simply receive this? However, it is absolutely impossible that this was sent by Zoran Krasic, absolutely impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Whatever the case may be, in the "inbox" of this person, there is a mention: "From Zoran Krasic," together with the attachment, so this may be someone who has used, on the 22nd of July, the computer to send this. Not much more can be said about this. Do you have another issue you'd like to address, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just this question, Mr. President. I believe that this is a very serious question. I am personally convinced that someone is doing this on purpose and that perhaps this is only the beginning, in order to compromise my legal advisers. You know that such things were done in 2006 and in the earlier years in order to compromise my Defence. You know that once my wife's visit was prohibited in relation to the conditions under which the wives of other detainees come to visit. This was based on the unverified claims made by the OTP that she is used by me as a channel for sending some kind of messages to the outside world. Whenever a rigorous measure is supposed to be taken against me, they plant or fabricate false evidence in order to corroborate their requests. I believe that this is part of an organised campaign that somebody is carrying out in anticipation of a ruling to be taken by you in order to deny me the right to defend myself. I think that that is what is going on, and in that case members of The Hague Tribunal -- well, now I cannot identify whether it's the Registry or the OTP. Somebody from here is doing that in cahoots with certain secret services in Belgrade. I am convinced that that is what is happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Seselj, what you have just said is on the record. You know that you have in front of you a professional Bench that weighs up everything. We do not exclude perhaps that some people are perhaps put in a difficult position. This is why we have this adversarial system. We listen to both sides and then we determine the matter. We are extremely careful and vigilant, of course. If there is any material element, we can conduct further investigations. We have resources to do this, and maybe we will follow this route, and all alternatives need to be addressed. And before we reach a conclusion, we of course are not entitled to make any mistakes. Since we are not entitled to make any mistakes, all the more reason to be extremely cautious, and this is exactly what we do. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... addressed this earlier. I just wondered whether as we had requested the admission of the three statements of the previous witness, we should have MFI numbers given to these statements so we don't lose track of them. The 65 ter numbers, if Your Honours would like me to repeat them, would be 65 ter number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we'll give an MFI number, but it's not because you have an MFI number that the document is admitted. This is just a number which enables you to identify the document. We have three statements, one in 2004, two in 2006. Registrar, can we have an MFI number, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 65 and 7266.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The statement which is 65 ter number 7265 will be Exhibit number MFI P526. The statement which is 65 ter number 7264 will be MFI P527, and the statement that's 65 ter number 7266 will be MFI P528.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In regard to what Mr. Marcussen said, I also have something to add to what I said about his request, his motion. These three statements should by no means be admitted into evidence, as any kind of evidence, but they can be additional proof in my criminal report against Carla Del Ponte, Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff and Daniel Saxon, and my later criminal report against Paolo Stocchi. It can be supporting evidence for that, showing what methods the Prosecution is using, where it's for the Prosecution to tender what they composed themselves and what the witness denies is his authentic statement, and denies consistently, cannot go into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're not going to go any further into this. Just a reminder of a technical nature. Witness 48 was not involved in any of these complaints. This is what I needed to say. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, the filings that relates to this particular issue by the accused, I believe, are all confidential filings, so I wonder whether we should redact the transcript making reference to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The contents, yes, but everybody knows now, for a long time already, that Mr. Seselj has filed motions about this. I think everybody knows about this. No secret. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to say my motions are not confidential, because they were published at the moment when I filed them, first on my web site, then later in one of my books. The responses from the Prosecution are confidential, and the decisions of the Trial Chamber are confidential. I did not mention them, but the contents of my motions became known to the public as I filed them. And now to deny to the public that they exist is really pointless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, as you know, we shall meet again at the end of August. This will be on a Tuesday. I don't know if it will be on Tuesday morning or Tuesday afternoon, but you will be informed about this. In the meantime, I wish everyone a good rest, and we shall meet again, Mr. Seselj, at the end of August. The Court stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 26th day of August, 2008.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.49 a.m.,
